A Costas array of order $n$ is a permutation matrix of size $n \times n$ such that the displacement vectors between any two pairs of 1s are distinct.
Specifically, if the positions of the 1s are $(r_1, c_1), (r_2, c_2), \dots, (r_n, c_n)$, then for any distinct pairs of indices $\{i, j\}$ and $\{k, l\}$, if $(r_i - r_j, c_i - c_j) = (r_k - r_l, c_k - c_l)$, then $\{i, j\} = \{k, l\}$.
Since it's a permutation, we can represent the array by a list $x$ of length $n$, where $x[c]$ is the row index of the mark in column $c$. The columns are $0, \dots, n-1$ and rows are $0, \dots, n-1$.
The condition is that for all $c_1, c_2, c_3, c_4$ with $c_1 < c_2$ and $c_3 < c_4$, if $(x[c_2] - x[c_1], c_2 - c_1) = (x[c_4] - x[c_3], c_4 - c_3)$, then $c_1 = c_3$ and $c_2 = c_4$.
